hints: Focus on what must be present for sodium carbonate to give off carbon dioxide, think acid reacting with carbonate.
Consider how each chloride behaves in water, SiCl4 and PCl5 hydrolyse fully to give strong HCl while AlCl3 hydrolyses to give H3O+.
Compare MgCl2 with AlCl3, the lower charge density of Mg2+ means its solution is almost neutral and too weak to release CO2, so check which combination fits.
walkthrough:
**Spot the real test - acidity**

Sodium carbonate gives $\text{CO}_2$ only with acids. The reaction is carbonate plus H+ to give CO2 and water.

$$\text{CO}_3^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Hydrolysis of SiCl4 and PCl5**

These covalent chlorides react violently and completely with water to form HCl, a strong acid.

$$\text{SiCl}_4 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Si(OH)}_4 + 4\text{HCl}$$
$$\text{PCl}_5 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 5\text{HCl}$$

**Hydrolysis of AlCl3 and MgCl2**

$\text{AlCl}_3$ dissolves to give $[\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ which loses a proton because the small, highly charged $\text{Al}^{3+}$ polarises water strongly. This gives an acidic solution of pH about 3.

$$[\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons [\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{OH})]^{2+} + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$$

**Decide which release CO2**

Solutions 1, 3 and 4 are acidic enough to protonate carbonate and fizz with $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$. $\text{MgCl}_2$ gives $[\text{Mg}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ which is only very weakly acidic and does not liberate $\text{CO}_2$. So only 1, 3 and 4 qualify.

options.A: Incorrect. While 1 is correct, 2 is not. MgCl2 gives an almost neutral solution, not acidic enough to release CO2 from carbonate. This option also misses the strongly acidic 3 and 4.
options.B: Incorrect. 3 and 4 are correct because they form HCl on hydrolysis, but 1 is also correct. Al3+ hydrolyses to give H3O+ and will also fizz with sodium carbonate.
options.C: Correct. AlCl3 gives an acidic hexaaqua ion solution, and SiCl4 and PCl5 hydrolyse completely to give HCl (plus silicic acid and phosphoric acid). All three are acidic enough to react with Na2CO3 to give CO2, while MgCl2 is not.
options.D: Incorrect. This is the trap of assuming all chlorides give acidic solutions. MgCl2 (2) is the exception, its lower charge density means negligible hydrolysis, so no CO2 is produced.
